answers.answer: The summary says the player(s) with the most Farmers gain a coin and the player(s) with the fewest lose a coin. It does not specify how ties or the unequal two-player case are handled.
answers.evidence: Census: ‘player(s) with the most Farmers gain a coin from the supply; the player(s) with the fewest lose a coin.’

answers.answer: The summary says the number drawn depends on Knight track advancement, starting at 4. It does not state whether a player must draw the full allowance, how Market spaces constrain drawing, or what happens to unused Market Followers.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: ‘draws Followers from their bag (number depends on Knight track advancement, starting at 4).’

answers.answer: The summary does not state whether actions may be partly filled across rounds, executed before full activation, or saved after activation. It only says players place drawn Followers on action spaces and that assigned Followers return to the bag after executing planned actions.
answers.evidence: Planning: ‘players place drawn Followers on action spaces’; Actions: ‘After executing, assigned Followers return to the bag.’

answers.answer: The summary says action execution begins with the Start Player and players execute their planned actions in any order. It does not explain alternating individual actions, passing, whether a player can act again after passing, or the status of an unused activation.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: ‘Starting with the Start Player, each player executes their planned actions (in any order).’

answers.answer: Farmhouse requires a Farmer and Boatman, advances the Farmer track, and gains a new Farmer tile. The destination of the recruited tile is not stated explicitly; the general bag-building reference says new Followers gained from action spaces enter your bag.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Farmhouse | Farmer + Boatman | Advance Farmer track; gain a new Farmer tile’; Player Reference: ‘New Followers gained from action spaces enter your bag.’

answers.answer: Village requires a Farmer and Craftsman and advances the Craftsman track to gain a Craftsman tile. The summary does not list three recruitable professions or distinct track rewards for each.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Village | Farmer + Craftsman | Advance Craftsman track; gain a new Craftsman tile.’

answers.answer: The summary says Technology tiles provide permanent advantages, including reducing Follower requirements, but does not say whether a newly recruited Craftsman can help another action in the same Action Phase, what the first Technology must replace, or placement limits.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: ‘Technology tiles: Provide permanent advantages (reduce Follower requirements, gain bonuses).’

answers.answer: The summary says Trader-track advancement is not described. It does not specify allowed Place categories, whether players may inspect stacks, or the first advance restriction.
answers.evidence: The Actions table mentions ‘Place a Place tile’ for Scriptorium but provides no category or stack rules.

answers.answer: University requires Farmer + Trader and advances the Scholar track to gain a Scholar tile; Castle requires Farmer + Knight and advances the Knight track to gain a Knight tile; Monastery requires Farmer + Scholar and advances the Monk track to gain a Monk tile. The general reference says recruits enter the bag. The fourth-Knight and last-track-space rules are not specified.
answers.evidence: Actions table lists the three actions and recruits; Player Reference: ‘New Followers gained from action spaces enter your bag.’

answers.answer: The summary says Monks are wild and can substitute for any Follower type. It does not explain whether this applies to ordinary actions, whether Knights or Technology can replace a required Monk, or substitutions on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: ‘Monks are wild and can substitute for any Follower type.’

answers.answer: Shipping moves the Merchant along waterways and Wagon moves it along roads; goods on the map are collected when the Merchant passes through. The summary does not specify the exact movement unit, whether multiple goods on one connection can be taken, or use of an empty connection.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Shipping ... Move Merchant along waterways’; ‘Wagon ... Move Merchant along roads’; Special Rules: ‘Goods on the map are collected when your Merchant passes through.’

answers.answer: The summary says Guildhall gains a Technology tile and that Trading Stations are placed in cities when the Merchant visits. It does not specify Guildhall's location requirement, whether opponents' cities are allowed, or the Orléans exception.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Guildhall ... Gain a Technology tile’; Special Rules: ‘Trading Stations: Placed in cities when your Merchant visits.’

answers.answer: The summary says Scriptorium builds a Place tile. It gives no details about Development movement or rewards/status changes for coin, Citizen, or status spaces.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Scriptorium ... Build a Place tile.’

answers.answer: The summary says Town Hall advances the Development track and places Followers on Beneficial Deeds. It says Followers sent there are removed permanently and can claim Citizen tiles worth VP. It does not specify minimum/maximum Followers, whether starting colored Followers may be used, rewards and destinations, Canalization, or completing a Deed.
answers.evidence: Actions table: ‘Town Hall | Various | Advance Development track; place Followers on Beneficial Deeds’; Special Rules: ‘Players can send Followers here permanently ... to claim Citizen tiles worth VP.’

answers.answer: The summary says the Pilgrimage tile is on top of the shuffled Hour Glass tiles at setup and events are applied in Phase 1 and executed in Phase 6. It does not state what Pilgrimage forbids or when it applies. The summary identifies no opening event beyond the setup statement that Pilgrimage is on top.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Shuffle Hour Glass tiles, place face down with Pilgrimage tile on top’; Phases 1 and 6 describe applying and executing the event.

answers.answer: The summary does not describe Harvest, eligible goods, where paid food goes, or what happens when a player has no food and fewer than five coins.
answers.evidence: The summary lists goods and coins but contains no Harvest rules.

answers.answer: The summary does not describe Plague, losses of neutral or colored Followers, destinations of lost pieces, track changes, or replacement draws.
answers.evidence: The summary contains no Plague rules.

answers.answer: The summary does not describe torture payments, payment choices, restrictions on sacrificing Followers or Development Points, or destinations of lost items.
answers.evidence: The summary contains no torture rules.

answers.answer: The summary does not state what happens when Character, Technology, or Goods Tile stock is unavailable, whether an action can resume later, or how temporary coin-supply shortages are handled.
answers.evidence: No stock-shortage or coin-supply exception appears in the summary.

answers.answer: The summary says highest total VP wins, and mentions coins, goods, Trading Stations, Citizens, and Development track scoring. It does not specify tie resolution, the bonus Citizen for tied station counts, values of the five goods, station/Citizen scoring formula, or final-score tie-break.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘Coins | 1 VP each’; ‘Goods tiles | Value printed on tile’; station points from Development track; ‘Citizens collected | Points per citizen’; ‘Highest total VP wins.’
